title: Orbital Debris and Space Governance Gaps
bottleneck: Low Earth orbit is filling with satellites and debris under a governance regime (the 1967 Outer Space Treaty) that assigns liability loosely and mandates no debris removal. Collision risk grows with each mega-constellation launch, and no binding traffic management or cleanup obligation exists. No state wants to pay for cleanup while others free-ride, the classic commons problem in orbit.
why_it_blocks: An unmanaged orbital commons risks Kessler-syndrome cascades that could deny space access for generations. Once cascading collisions begin, no cleanup technology can restore safe orbits quickly.
current_state: Voluntary guidelines and national licensing help marginally; active debris removal has no funded international program. A binding traffic-management treaty has been discussed for decades without progress. Without action, the orbital commons will keep degrading with each launch.
